correctness.rationale: For every 2<=k<=n-2 the primitive normal rays at each k-subset vertex form one n-ray circuit with two signs of sizes k and n-k. The two triangulations have cones obtained by omitting one ray, whose n-1 signed coordinate rays are integral bases. All proper faces are smooth, so choices glue independently and smallness excludes new rays. Toric support heights on the 2n original rays give circuit bends sum_{j in B}(a_j+b_j)-sum_i b_i, exactly the k-subset-sum arrangement. Relative strict convexity and ampleness of the projective target make the chamber criterion necessary and sufficient. The Gorenstein test is the sum-zero dual lattice equation. The standalone exact checker verifies local determinants and independently evaluates 46 and 332 using the Whitney-Zaslavsky formula; general conclusions follow from proofs, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: The newly isolated statement is the global count of smooth torus-equivariant small resolutions over all hypersimplex normal-fan varieties and its if-and-only-if projectivity criterion via a subset-sum arrangement. Historical work already gives rank-one cone singularities and Gorenstein behavior; these inputs are not claimed new. Wang--Yu supplies this exact toric family but addresses cohomology, while Deshpande--Menon--Singh supplies the threshold arrangement and the already-known 46/332 counts without their toric-resolution interpretation. Literature searches and available historical claims revealed no implication that encompasses the new global classification. Secondary-fan reformulations remain a material residual risk.
residual_risks: A secondary-fan, Mori-dream-space, or variation-of-GIT source not identified here may already state an equivalent geometric chamber classification.
General toric circuit subdivision techniques make the argument short; the novelty lies in the exact natural family and the global criterion, not those standard tools.
Current comparison covers accessible primary material and available historical records, not every possible earlier work.

value.rationale: This is a complete birational-geometric classification for a natural infinite family (generic torus orbit closures in Grassmannians). It distinguishes projective from nonprojective smooth small resolutions, provides exact finite counts and a general chamber counting mechanism, identifies all exceptional fibers, and for k=2 connects toric birational models to labeled threshold graphs. In particular 18 of 64 small resolutions of the octahedral hypersimplex toric threefold are provably nonprojective. This structural projectivity boundary is not merely re-evaluating an existing table.
